html:
The Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico opened in 1963 with a radio dish 305 metres across, set in a natural sinkhole in the karst hills. For more than fifty years it was the largest single dish telescope in the world.

Its scientists measured the rotation of Mercury, discovered the first binary pulsar, which won the Nobel prize for physics in 1993, and found the first planets outside the solar system, around a pulsar. In 1974 it beamed a message toward a star cluster.

The dish appeared in films such as GoldenEye and Contact. Weakened by age and by storms such as Hurricane Maria, its cables failed and the platform crashed into the dish in December 2020. It was not rebuilt. It had been a pride of Puerto Rico and a site of the Cold War science race.
